news.title: 新任苹果CEO约翰·特努斯必须提升苹果产品中的人工智能应用
news.snippet: 苹果新任CEO的任命引发了关于公司AI战略和产品智能化升级的重大问题。
news.raw_snippet: # The appointment of Apple’s new CEO raises some big questions. If the tech giant’s golden run of growth is to continue, then the handover from Tim Cook to successor John Ternus must shed more light on the firm’s AI strategy. There’s a neat bit of symmetry in the fact that Apple and Berkshire Hathaway are both in the midst of chief executive transitions that will define their next three decades. At Berkshire, Greg Abel has just taken over running the world’s most famous conglomerate from the world’s most famous investor, Warren Buffett. A profile of Abel in *The* *Wall Street Journal* this week – complete with photos of a frail Buffett – painted a picture of a company in a state of mild but predictable flux, as Abel gently tries to put his stamp on a business Buffett had run in a decidedly idiosyncratic way for 55 years. news.title: 科技CEO们认为AI将让他们同时无处不在
news.snippet: 科技行业领导者相信人工智能技术将使他们实现全方位实时管理，突破物理空间限制。
news.raw_snippet: # Tech CEOs Think AI Will Let Them Be Everywhere at Once. On April 13, the Financial Times reported that Meta is working up a photorealistic, three-dimensional AI avatar of chief exec Mark Zuckerberg, according to several people at the company. Meanwhile, Jack Dorsey, CEO of Block (formerly Square), has overseen rolling layoffs as the financial services company leans more heavily into AI. Responding to a request for comment on Dorsey’s remarks, a Block spokesperson provided a link to a March 31 blog post Dorsey coauthored with Sequoia partner Roelof Botha, titled “From Hierarchy to Intelligence.” The piece lays out a case for eliminating middle management by rethinking how AI is integrated into the workflow. “Most companies using AI today are giving everyone a copilot, which makes the existing structure work slightly better without changing it,” the pair writes. “We’re after something different: a company built as an intelligence (or mini-AGI).” Artificial general intelligence, or AGI, is an as-yet-nonexistent kind of reasoning AI that matches or exceeds human capabilities.

news.raw_snippet: With Tim Cook moving into the executive chairman role and John Ternus stepping in as CEO, attention now turns to how Apple balances its established hardware and services franchise with its push on AI across the ecosystem. The CEO transition from Tim Cook to John Ternus comes at a time when Apple is tightly linking its hardware roadmap with AI features and services. Ternus has been responsible for the hardware behind products like iPhone, Mac and wearables, which sit at the core of Apple’s AI plans and future devices such as the reported AI-powered smart glasses.
